PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and ongoing management of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment one month after his last visit. He reports that his dyspnea has remained stable, with no exacerbations since the previous consultation. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler about four to five times daily, which he notes is a slight improvement from the previous month. He remains compliant with his inhaled corticosteroids and continues to engage actively in pulmonary rehabilitation sessions, which he finds increasingly beneficial for his respiratory status and overall well-being.
Despite his adherence to a low-sodium diet and ongoing furosemide therapy at 100 mg daily, Mr. Fairfax's bilateral lower extremity edema has not improved. He describes the edema as 1+ pitting, unchanged from last month, and maintains a regimen of leg elevation, although he has not observed any significant alleviation of the swelling. He denies any associated symptoms such as shortness of breath or chest discomfort related to the edema.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience profound fatigue, which he describes as debilitating. He acknowledges that while his mood has improved slightly due to increased therapy sessions, he still encounters episodes of anxiety. He has remained consistent with his sertraline regimen, which he believes has contributed to a modest improvement in his depressive symptoms, although he expresses a desire for more substantial progress.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using four to five times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (ongoing management). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 76, BP 128/78, RR 18, O2 sat 90% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress, appears fatigued but alert. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.1, Hgb 10.6, Hct 32.0, Plt 215 2. BMP: Na 134, K 4.1, Cl 97, CO2 25, BUN 28, Cr 1.4, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 580 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status remains stable. He is encouraged to persist with pulmonary rehabilitation and strict adherence to inhaled corticosteroids. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema continues to be managed with furosemide. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended to evaluate renal function further due to the slight increase in creatinine. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Mr. Fairfax has reported minor improvements in anxiety and depressive symptoms, and ongoing psychological support is encouraged. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
